options: Whether the subquery returns at least one row — TRUE or FALSE
The total count of rows the subquery returns
Whether a specific column value is NULL
Whether the subquery returns exactly one row
questions.explain: EXISTS is purely a presence test — it doesn't care about the actual data returned.

questions.q: Why does 'SELECT 1' inside an EXISTS subquery work the same as 'SELECT *'?
options: EXISTS never looks at what columns the subquery returns, only whether any row comes back at all
They actually behave differently — SELECT 1 is faster but less accurate
SELECT 1 converts the result to a boolean automatically
SELECT 1 is required syntax and SELECT * would cause an error
questions.explain: This is why SELECT 1 is a common T-SQL convention inside EXISTS — the selected columns are irrelevant.

questions.q: Why is NOT EXISTS safer than NOT IN when NULL values might be present?
options: NOT EXISTS never compares individual values — it only asks whether any row matched, avoiding the NULL trap entirely
NOT EXISTS converts NULL to zero before comparing
NOT EXISTS and NOT IN behave identically in every case
NOT EXISTS automatically filters out NULL values before comparing
questions.explain: This directly solves the NOT IN NULL trap from Lesson 53, since EXISTS-based logic never does a value-by-value comparison.

questions.q: Why does this course recommend preferring NOT EXISTS over NOT IN?
options: NOT IN is deprecated and no longer works in modern SQL Server
There is no real reason — they are always interchangeable
NOT EXISTS is required syntax and NOT IN is invalid
Whenever the subquery's column might contain NULL — which is most of the time unless verified otherwise
questions.explain: This is a practical safety default given how easy it is to overlook a NULL possibility.

questions.q: Why does EXISTS often perform better than IN on large tables?
options: IN always scans the entire table twice
EXISTS can stop scanning the moment it finds one matching row, rather than needing to enumerate every match
There is no performance difference between EXISTS and IN
EXISTS never actually executes the subquery
questions.explain: This short-circuiting behavior is why EXISTS is often the faster choice, a topic revisited in the Performance Tuning chapter.
